Our roots run deep

Behind every Kissan,
there’s a kisan.

Good food starts with the people who grow it.

A journey from farm to family.

Kissan’s name comes from a Punjab railway stop where farmers sold freshly harvested fruit during the British era. That local meeting place grew into a familiar name in Indian homes.

1950

The UB Group, led by Vittal Mallya, acquired Kissan from Mitchell Bros.

1993

Brooke Bond India acquired Kissan. The brand is now part of Hindustan Unilever.

Today

Jams, sauces, peanut butter and squash bring farm ingredients to everyday meals.

Growing together.

Kissan’s early innovations included canned fruit, vegetables and baked beans. Its work later focused on helping small farmers produce quality ingredients.

HUL’s partnership with the Maharashtra Government for sustainable tomato sourcing started in 2012 and became self-sustaining in 2015. HUL continued providing a produce buy-back guarantee, alongside guidance on seeds, irrigation and agricultural practices.

The brand’s published history reports that 76% of its ketchup tomatoes came from sustainable sources in 2019, with around 8,000 farmers growing tomatoes for HUL that year. One introduced variety could be harvested in 90 days, compared with 150–180 days for traditional varieties, and its brighter red colour helped farmers obtain better prices.

Ingredients with a sense of place.

Nagpur oranges. Lemons from the Himalayan foothills. Kerala pineapples. Karnataka grapes. Gujarat peanuts. Kissan’s range connects familiar flavours with farms across India.

The farmers behind these ingredients remain central to the Kissan story.
